question: A distribution center had 172 packages. He multiplied by 8 for batch processing. Then multiplied by 9. Then multiplied by 7 for volume. Then 39247 were subtracted for distribution (first wave). Then 15261 more were subtracted (second wave). He added 21. A backup facility had 84 packages (not counted). What was the final count?
In the morning, a shop had 75 items. They added 12. They removed 20. They removed 7. By afternoon, they added 77. There was a distractor of 50 items. By evening, they removed 102. How many items?
A baker had 65 cookies. She added 8 more. She multiplied by 8. She added 12 additional cookies. She removed 196. How many cookies?

In the morning, a toy drive had 118 stuffed animals collected. By midday, 87 stuffed animals were donated to a children's hospital. In the afternoon, a local business donated 54 more stuffed animals. That evening, 58 stuffed animals were sent to a shelter. Right after that, the remaining stuffed animals tripled when a toy company matched the donation drive. Before the night was over, 25 more were given to a school event, and 18 more went to a family shelter downtown. How many stuffed animals were left after the family shelter donation?

On Sunday morning Freya had 61 raffle prizes on the table, more than her co-organiser Sam had gathered. Before noon 28 prizes were claimed. At midday a shop donated 56 prizes, and Sam brought 51 more in the early afternoon. Later a bakery added 47 prizes. During the evening draw 127 prizes were handed out. How many prizes are left on the table?

A cobbler had 20 pairs of laces in his drawer and used 18 pairs on Monday's repairs. A supplier delivered 63 pairs on Tuesday. A closing-down shop sold him 55 pairs, and a market stall added another 71 pairs. Half of the drawer is taken up by tins of polish. The shop opens at 8 every morning. How many pairs of laces are in the drawer?

A business had 130 orders initially. They added 75 through promotions. Then removed 329 for cancellation (in dollars of lost revenue). The count multiplied by 4. Then multiplied by 9. Finally, divided by 4 to create fulfillment batches. A competitor processed 1000 orders but separate fulfillment. How many batches to fulfill all orders?
A warehouse had 191 boxes. They removed 64. They removed 123 more. They added 55 back. They multiplied by 9. How many boxes total?

On Monday morning a fruit stall opened with 40 ripe mangoes on the counter, and a neighbouring grower brought over 14 more before the first customers arrived. During the afternoon the owner cut every mango on the counter into 8 slices for his tasting bowls. By early evening 402 of those slices had been sold to passers-by, and a late delivery from the packing shed added another 34 slices to the bowls. Overnight the supplier tripled the number of slices ready for the next morning's market. How many slices are ready for the morning market?

A production line had 140 units. It multiplied by 7 (shift boost). Then by 7 more (efficiency gain). The count was divided by 5 (split into groups). By midday, 401 units were removed. By afternoon, 769 more units were lost. By evening, 24 units arrived. When converted to dozens (unit change), how many dozen units remained?

In the morning a chocolate factory's crew of a dozen workers packed 146 boxes for shipping. In the afternoon they packed 32 more boxes. Every box holds 9 cartons, every carton holds 7 packs, every pack holds 4 bars, and every bar is scored into 8 squares. In the evening the auditor spent ninety minutes, an hour and a half, checking the whole shipment square by square. How many squares of chocolate did the day's boxes contain in total?

A puzzle company had 114 boxes of jigsaw puzzles in a warehouse. A late shipment added 5 more boxes. Then 5 boxes were damaged in a forklift accident and discarded. A big wholesale order then shipped out 112 boxes to a retailer. A new production run turned every remaining box into 6 boxes. The stock then tripled again when a second production line came online. How many boxes of jigsaw puzzles were in the warehouse after the second production line came online?

A small library starts the semester with 46 dollars in its book-fair cash box, which comes out to 4600 cents. The librarian spends 19 dollars restocking bookmarks and pencils for the fair. A batch of overdue fines waived for a promotion then costs the fund another 16 dollars. A parent donation adds 48 dollars to the box. A raffle at the fair brings in 69 more dollars. A final matching gift from the school board adds 64 dollars to the total. A dozen extra raffle tickets were printed just in case, though that number plays no role in the cash total. How many dollars are in the book-fair cash box now?

The library's mystery section began the day with 118 books checked out. A morning return dropped that number by 7. A cataloging fix then doubled the official checkout count when duplicate holds were resolved. An afternoon return event brought the count down by 65. A book club sign-up doubled the checkout count once more. A branch-wide sync multiplied that number by 9 to combine it with identical sister-branch totals. Finally, an evening rush added 67 more checkouts to the tally. For her report, the librarian converted the checkout period from two weeks into 14 days, a simple unit change unrelated to the tally. The reference section, unrelated to this tally, had 300 books checked out separately that day. How many checkouts did the combined tally show by the end of the day?

A farm starts with 74 animals. In the morning, 7 leave (67). By afternoon, 55 arrive (122). By evening, 36 more come (158). They gain 78 (236). They gain 58 (294). At least double 50 would be 100. How many animals does the farm have?

In the morning the diner had 177 pints of chowder and sold 78 pints. In the afternoon 7 pints were spilled and 34 pints were sold. In the evening the rest was served in cups, at 2 cups to a pint. How many cups of chowder were served?

On Tuesday morning a printer received 126 reels of paper, and each reel was cut into 4 rolls. Before noon every roll was slit into 7 ribbons. In the afternoon the ribbons were shared equally between the 6 presses, and the evening press is the one being followed. That press then printed 6 tickets from every ribbon in its share. Late that night a partner shop sent over 74 finished tickets. The works covers 700 square metres, and the presses are timed in minutes although the schedule is written in hours. How many tickets does the evening press have?

Ingrid grows more sunflowers than her neighbour Bo does. She started with 236 seedlings, and 157 were lost to slugs. Bo gave her 42 seedlings from his own tray. Every seedling she had left went on to produce 6 flower heads. Wind snapped 207 of the flower heads before the show. How many flower heads does Ingrid have?
A factory starts with 231 items. It loses 134 (97). It multiplies by 9 (873). It multiplies by 8 (6984). It adds 65 (7049). It adds 15 (7064). It loses 5093 (1971). Half of 10 is 5. How many items?

A council bought 7 crates of laptops for its schools, each crate holding 106 laptops. The supplier then delivered 3 times that many for the whole borough. The laptops were shared equally between the 6 districts, and one district took its share. The borough has 45 schools. That district's allocation was later increased to 3 times its size by a government grant. A charity then added 69 laptops to the district's total. How many laptops does the district have?

Two cousins, Ana and Beto, collect seashells, but this story follows only Ana's collection, which started at 40 shells that morning, well ahead of Beto's count. In the morning, a beach trip left her with 3 times as many shells. In the afternoon, a swap meet with other collectors multiplied her shells by 9. That evening, a friend gave her 8 more shells found near the pier. A local shop was selling shell necklaces for 22 dollars each, unrelated to her count. Finally, a matching gift from her grandmother doubled her shells once more. How many shells did Ana end up with by the end of the evening?

A warehouse starts with 64 items. They multiply by 8 for eight distribution locations. They lose 406 items to fulfillment. They add 14 items from recovery. They multiply by 5 to forecast five weeks. What is their five-week inventory?

Ryan started with 86 points. He earned 6 points. He lost 90 points in a penalty. He then multiplied by 8 times due to a bonus round. He lost 5 points. He gained 69 points from winning. He multiplied again by 8 times for final scoring. His teammate had double his points. Someone else had 400 points but that's not tracked here. How many points does Ryan have at the end?

A tech company started the morning with 213 software patches. They multiplied workload by 9 for deployment. They added 26 patches from new bug reports. They multiplied the total by 3 for all servers. They removed 1322 patches from old systems. They removed another 3738 patches during cleanup. How many patches remained in the system?

A choir had 72 music folders and sent 16 of them away to be rebound. Half of the folders that remained went to the tenors and half to the basses. The tenors were then given 23 more folders by a retiring member. A neighbouring choir lent them another 19, and the librarian found 11 in the vestry cupboard. How many folders do the tenors have now?
